summary: Reduces each input CHOP channel to a one-sample analysis value such as average, maximum, minimum, sum, RMS power, peak value, peak index, or duplicate counts. Usually followed by Math CHOP for range shaping.

key_params.name: function
key_params.note: Analysis operation such as average, maximum, minimum, sum, RMS power, or peak modes.

key_params.name: allowstart
key_params.note: Allow the first sample to count as a peak.

key_params.name: allowend
key_params.note: Allow the last sample to count as a peak.

key_params.name: nopeakvalue
key_params.note: Sentinel output value when no peaks are found.

key_params.name: valleys
key_params.note: Analyze valleys instead of peaks for corresponding functions.

key_params.name: autoexportroot
key_params.note: Export root for path-style channel names.

common_gotchas: Analyze CHOP output is one sample long and can collapse many samples to one value, so preserve or smooth upstream detail before analysis if needed.
Peak Index results are sample indices and the first sample is 0; convert or normalize them before using them as UI or visual ranges.
No Peak Value defaults to -1, so downstream Math CHOP mappings should handle that sentinel when no peak is found.
Choose peak versus valley analysis intentionally; Analyze Valleys vs Peaks changes the meaning of the same menu functions.
For live audio, confirm the upstream CHOP is cooking and producing nonzero channels before trusting the analysis value.
